title: Will there be a lunar base by the end of 2029?
criteria: Any permanent lunar infrastructure complete enough that humans could live there for a few weeks; people need not actually reside there. No local-resource self-sufficiency requirement.
why: A few-weeks-habitable permanent lunar base by 2029 is much easier than the milestone's continuously crewed 12-month, locally self-sustaining lunar-or-Martian base, so success supplies a lower-bound event.

title: Will there be a fusion reactor generating electricity commercially by the end of 2035?
criteria: By the deadline, a fusion reactor must connect to an electrical grid, sell electricity commercially, and maintain net-positive energy output; prototypes not selling electricity do not count. No explicit three-consecutive-month duration.
why: Commercial grid sales with net-positive operation is close to the milestone, but the market omits its three-month sustained-output requirement, making it the easier event and a lower-bound indicator.

title: Will Helion Energy deliver 50 MW of fusion-generated electricity to Microsoft before 2029?
criteria: Helion must publicly document a commercial 50 MW generator, net-energy gain, grid connection, and delivery of at least 50 MW to Microsoft before 2029.
why: This asks about one named supplier and a 50 MW contract by 2028, not the first plant meeting the milestone's sustained three-month public-grid criterion; another company could satisfy the milestone first.

title: By Dec 31, 2035, will any nuclear fusion power plant have delivered at least 100 MW of net electrical power, 30 day ave.
criteria: Any fusion plant must deliver at least 100 MWe net to a public grid or external users, averaged over a continuous 30-day window.
why: The 100 MWe/30-day threshold is much higher than the milestone's unspecified output, while the milestone requires three months rather than one; neither event strictly implies the other.
